notes: §1985:VII.4.2.2 prints CLOSE { file-name-1 [ { REEL | UNIT } [ FOR REMOVAL ] | WITH { NO REWIND | LOCK } ] } ..., with WITH and FOR the only words not underlined. closeStatement is CLOSE closeFilePhrase+, closeFilePhrase is fileName closeOption? and closeOption is (REEL | UNIT) (FOR? REMOVAL)? | WITH? NO REWIND | WITH? LOCK, so each file-name takes at most one of the two alternatives of the bracket; BindClose resolves each name through ResolveFile (COBOL1639 for a name that is no file) and binds one close per file-name in source order with the written form (ReelUnit, ReelUnitForRemoval, NoRewind, WithLock), which EmitClose hands to the run time. The 1985 edition keeps WITH LOCK through VisitCloseOption, which is silent below 2023 and refuses the phrase there (COBOL0902). Probed at 85: every spelling of the format compiles (REEL, UNIT, REEL FOR REMOVAL, UNIT REMOVAL, WITH NO REWIND, NO REWIND, WITH LOCK, LOCK, a list with a different phrase per file, with and without commas); REEL WITH NO REWIND, REEL WITH LOCK, NO REWIND LOCK, LOCK WITH NO REWIND, FOR REMOVAL without REEL, REEL UNIT, WITH alone, WITH REWIND, CLOSE with no file-name and a record-name or undefined operand are refused; REEL and NO REWIND on a relative file are refused (COBOL1693, the relative format has neither) while WITH LOCK on it compiles. At run time CLOSE WITH LOCK gives status 00 and the next OPEN 38; CLOSE REEL, UNIT FOR REMOVAL and WITH NO REWIND on a disk file give status 07; the file stays open after REEL or UNIT (a WRITE that follows gives 00) and is closed by WITH NO REWIND (the witness reopens it). The witness closes one file WITH NO REWIND and one plainly, compiles REEL and UNIT FOR REMOVAL, closes two files WITH LOCK and shows status 38 on the reopen through a USE procedure.

next.reason: §1985:VII.4.2.2 gives each file-name either {REEL | UNIT} [FOR REMOVAL] or WITH {NO REWIND | LOCK}; §1985:VII.4.2.4 GR3's table gives 'CLOSE WITH LOCK' its effect E ('The file is locked and cannot be opened again'). §2023:14.9.6.2 keeps {REEL | UNIT} [FOR REMOVAL] and 'WITH NO REWIND' but has no LOCK alternative, so CLOSE f WITH LOCK, conforming in 1985, is refused at compile time (not an exception condition). The 2023 format is the CLOSE of every organization, and §2023:14.9.6.3 SR1 ('The NO REWIND, REEL, and UNIT phrases may be used only with files that are of sequential organization') and SR2 ('The words REEL and UNIT are equivalent') state the rest of what the 1985 sequential format shows. Narrower: CHANGED.
